question: Which of the adverse effects reported is characteristic of dihydropyridines ?:

options.opb: Muscle cramps, located preferably in the extremities.
options.opc: Peripheral edema, located preferably in the legs.
options.opd: Dry cough, which remits when interrupting the treatment.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Dihydropyridines -> calcium channel blockers -> peripheral vasodilation -> peripheral edema -> located preferably in the legs -> 80% CHAIN: Dihydropyridines -> calcium channel blockers -> minimal effect on cardiac tissue -> less likely to cause bradycardia -> 70% CHAIN: Dihydropyridines -> calcium channel blockers -> less likely to cause bronchoconstriction -> 90% CHAIN: Dihydropyridines -> calcium channel blockers -> muscle cramps, located preferably in the extremities -> 50% CHAIN: Dihydropyridines -> calcium channel blockers -> less likely to cause dry cough -> 80%
analysis: Peripheral edema, located preferably in the legs, is a characteristic adverse effect reported with dihydropyridines due to their vasodilatory effects.
